primitives.name: Calibration Weight
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Calibration weights The blend weight was chosen by lowest 2024 mean absolute error and then frozen.
primitives.assumptions: The blend weight is selected based on the minimum 2024 Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and remains fixed for subsequent years (2025, 2026).
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the optimal 2024 MAE selection does not generalize to later years, the model's static weighting fails.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's cross-validation-based posterior calibration, where weights are derived from minimizing out-of-sample error.
layer2.telemetry: Validation accuracy on holdout data; consistency of MAE across training vs. test splits.

primitives.name: Position Weight
primitives.verbatim_quote: Position weights are the 2025 inverse MAE, normalized to sum to 1.
primitives.assumptions: Weights are inversely proportional to the 2025 projected Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for each position, ensuring they sum to one.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If the 2025 MAE estimates are inaccurate, the position weights will be incorrectly distributed, leading to biased projections.

layer2.mapping: Analogous to GSI's Bayesian posterior reweighting, where less reliable positions receive lower influence in the combined forecast.
layer2.telemetry: Sensitivity analysis of projection errors to weight perturbations; stability of normalized coefficients.

primitives.name: Projection Bias
primitives.verbatim_quote: A position that was harder to project gets less weight.
primitives.assumptions: Positions with higher inherent uncertainty (higher MAE) are down-weighted to reduce overall forecast bias, while the devigged-price baseline serves as a reference point for evaluating performance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When high-bias positions dominate the projection due to incorrect down-weighting, the combined forecast becomes systematically skewed.

layer2.mapping: Relates to GSI's conformal prediction framework, which adjusts for systematic bias by incorporating external baselines like the devigged price.
layer2.telemetry: Bias-variance trade-off diagnostics; deviation of predicted means from observed outcomes relative to the baseline.

primitives.name: Elo Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: This Elo does not beat that baseline, so the calibration contract must not come back VALIDATED.
primitives.assumptions: The Elo rating system's predictive power is assessed against a defined baseline (devigged-price = 0.2122); if it underperforms, the associated calibration contract is deemed invalid.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the Elo model consistently fails to outperform the baseline, its credibility as a predictive tool collapses.

layer2.mapping: Links to GSI's hypothesis testing paradigm, where a model's performance is statistically validated against a null hypothesis (the baseline).
layer2.telemetry: p-value calculation for performance difference; win/loss record of the Elo model versus the baseline.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is combining multiple probabilistic forecasts from different models (Elo, position-specific regressions) into a coherent blended projection. This requires accounting for heteroskedasticity (varying uncertainty across positions) and temporal drift (changing performance metrics over years). The calibration weight selects the best-performing year's blend, assuming stationarity, which may fail if underlying dynamics shift. Position weights invert MAE to correct for bias, but this assumes MAE is a sufficient measure of uncertainty, ignoring skewness and kurtosis. The validation step uses an external baseline to check for systematic underperformance, preventing overfitting to historical data. Overall, this forms a hierarchical Bayesian-like structure: first, individual model posteriors; second, weighted combination; third, external validation.
